content_of_post_to_answer: How much of our personality is shaped by childhood?
answer: Childhood shapes our personality less by deciding who we become and more by teaching us what feels normal. A child who learns that emotions are welcomed may grow into someone who expresses themselves easily; a child who learns that approval must be earned may become highly adaptable but struggle with authenticity. The interesting part is that these patterns are not fixed traits—they are strategies we developed to fit our early environment. Maturity often means noticing which childhood strategies still serve us and which ones we are carrying long after the original situation has disappeared.
